subsystems.name: Stretchable substrate and encapsulation
subsystems.role: a skin-thin, breathable base that holds the electronics and sticks comfortably to the body.
parts: elastomer film (e.g. PDMS or polyurethane, tens of micrometres thick)

subsystems.name: Biosensing layer
subsystems.role: measures vital signs and motion continuously.

subsystems.name: Sweat microfluidics and chemical sensors
subsystems.role: collects tiny amounts of sweat and reads biomarkers like glucose, lactate or electrolytes.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: runs the patch without a bulky battery, using body heat or movement.

subsystems.name: Flexible electronics and communication
subsystems.role: processes signals and sends data wirelessly to a phone or cloud.

buildSteps.title: Design the sensor layout
buildSteps.detail: Choose which vitals and biomarkers to measure, and arrange sensors so they sit over the right body locations.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the stretchable substrate
buildSteps.detail: Spin-coat or cast a thin elastomer film onto a temporary carrier, then cure it at low temperature.

buildSteps.title: Pattern sensors and conductors
buildSteps.detail: Print or photolithographically define stretchable conductive tracks, electrodes and sensing materials on the film.

buildSteps.title: Integrate microfluidics
buildSteps.detail: Bond moulded channels and reagent pads over the chemical sensors to route sweat.

buildSteps.title: Mount electronics
buildSteps.detail: Place flexible chips, antenna and power harvester, then encapsulate them in another elastomer layer.

buildSteps.title: Apply skin adhesive
buildSteps.detail: Laminate a breathable, medical-grade adhesive on the skin side, leaving sensor openings.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Run the patch on human volunteers, comparing readings against standard clinical instruments, then adjust algorithms.

prerequisites.why: they must bend and stretch with skin without cracking or losing conductivity.
body heat and motion give very little power, so the patch must sip microwatts.
the patch must stay on for days without irritation or allowing sweat to short the electronics.
sweat concentrations are tiny and vary with flow rate, so reliable calibration is hard.
standard NFC and Bluetooth chips already let small devices send data to phones.

pathway.milestone: lab prototypes that measure one or two signals at a time
pathway.unlocks: proof that skin-like sensors can work on real bodies.

pathway.milestone: multifunctional patches tested in clinical studies
pathway.unlocks: continuous monitoring of conditions like dehydration or heart arrhythmia.

pathway.milestone: first commercial patches for specific uses (e.g. wound healing or prosthetics)
pathway.unlocks: routine use in hospitals and at home.

pathway.milestone: autonomous, body-powered patches that close the loop with treatment
pathway.unlocks: proactive, personalised healthcare without bulky equipment.
